la:adj:devexus.html:
dēvexus, a, um, adj.
deveho
, of places,
inclining downwards, sloping, shelving, steep (class.—for syn. v. declivis).
Lit.: lucus Vestae, qui a Palatii radice in novam viam devexus est,; cf. : mundus in Austros,; and: devexus in planum,: ut de locis superioribus haec declivia et devexa cernebantur, * : arva,: margo (lacus), (with acclivus): Orion,i. e. towards his setting,; cf.: sol paulum a meridie, ap. ; and dies devexior,: globus devexior,.—Hence, subst.: dēvexum, i, n., an inclined surface, a slope: aqua in devexo fluit, in plano continetur et stagnat,.—
Transf., inclining, declining: aetas jam a diuturnis laboribus devexa ad otium,: aetas,: devexa et molliter desinens compositio,.—Absol.: per devexum ire,i. e. easily,

la:verb:deversor.gloss: to lodge or stay (as a guest)
senses: to lodge or stay (as a guest)
la:verb:deversor.html:
dē-versor (vorsor), ātus, 1,
v. dep. n., to be tarrying as a guest, to lodge anywhere as a guest (rare but good prose): cum Athenis apud eum deversarer,; so, apud aliquem,; : in domo aliqua,; cf. : domi suae deversatum esse,; ; fin.: parum laute,.

senses: to turn in, put up at, lodge
la:verb:deverto.html:
dē-verto or dēvorto, ti, sum (in MSS. often confounded with diverto), 3, v. a. and n.
Act.
To turn away, turn aside any thing: comites suo hortatu,: acies,: ventura fata suo cursu,; cf. .— Far more freq.,
Pass. with mid. force, to turn one's self aside; and with esp. reference to the term. ad quem, to turn or betake one's self to any place; to turn in, put up at (in the latter sense esp. freq. in Plaut., whereas Cicero commonly uses the act. form; v. under no. II.).
Prop.: si qui Cobiamacho (vico) deverterentur,: juvat ire jugis, qua nulla priorum Castaliam molli devertitur orbita clivo,: deverti ad amicos suos, Cato ap. Müll.: devortitur apud suum paternum hospitem,: apud aliquem,; so ; cf. ib. § 7: ad me in hospitium maximum,; cf. in amici hospitium,; : huc in tabernam,: intro domum,; cf. : in hortos in quibus devertebatur, pergunt,.—
Trop., to resort to, have recourse to (very rare): ad magicas artes,: meas ad artes,.—
Neutr. (i. q. no. I. B.), to turn or go aside from any place or any direction; to turn or go towards; to turn in, put up, lodge anywhere.
Prop.: viā devertit,: viā, Plin.

Pan. 52 fin.: devertere ad cauponem, ad hospitem,; : ad aliquem,; : ad villam Philemonis,; cf.: ad se in Albanum,: ad villam suam,: in villam suam,: domum regis hospitis,: Massiliam,; cf. Interamnam,: Rhodum, et saep.—With apud (late Lat.; cf. deversor): in pago apud familiares devertimus, Ap. M. 4 init.; cf. , p. 238, 14.—Absol.: itineris causa ut deverterem,.—

Trop. (very rare): sed redeamus illuc, unde devertimus,have digressed,; so : in haec devertisse non fuerit alienum, (Sillig, divertisse).
la:verb:deverto.inflection: ti, sum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:noun:deversoriolum.gloss: a small inn or lodging house
senses: a small inn or lodging house

la:adj:devius.html:
dē-vĭus, a, um, adj.
via
,
lying off the high-road; out of the way, devious (class.; for syn. cf.: avius, invius).
Lit.: iter,a by-way,; (cf. avius); : oppidum,: saltus,: calles,: rura,.—Subst.: dēvia, ōrum, n., lonely, unfrequented places: per aspera ac devia,: in devia terrarum,.—
Transf., of living beings dwelling in out-of-the-way places, retired, sequestered: Anagnini, cum essent devii, etc.,: gens,: montani,: civitas,: mihi devio nemus Mirari libet, wandering about in unfrequented places: : uxores (i. e. capellae),: scortum,i. e. retired, shy,: avis (i. e. the great owl, which dwells in lonely places), : equus,leaping aside,.—
Poet., inaccessible: limina,—
Trop., inconstant, erroneous, inconsistent, foolish: quid potest esse tam flexibile, tam devium, quam animus ejus, qui, etc.,: vita, id. Fragm. ap. : via,; : nihil quasi devium loqui,i. e. out of the way, impertinent,: noster Plato nihil ab hac secta vel paululum devius, Ap. : homo in omnibus consiliis praeceps et devius,; .—Poet. with gen.: devius aequi,; cf.: pectora recti,: devius promissi es, Mart. Cap. poet. 3 init.—Adv. does not occur.

la:verb:devincio.html:
dē-vincĭo, nxi, nctum, 4 (
perf. sync. devinxti, ), v. a., to bind fast, tie up (class.; esp. freq. in trop. signif.).
Lit.: servum,; cf. leonem,: Dircam ad taurum,: aliquem fasciis,; cf.: opercula plumbo,.—In Greek constr.: devinctus tempora lauro,encircled, crowned, et saep.—
Trop., to bind together, to unite closely; to engage, to oblige, lay under obligation: totam Italiam omnibus vinclis devinctam et constrictam teneretis,: illud vinculum, quod primum homines inter se rei publicae societate devinxit,; cf.: eloquentia nos juris, legum, urbium societate devinxit,: nec acervatim multa frequentans una complexione devinciet,; cf. ; : istoc me facto tibi devinxti,; so of laying under an obligation by kindness, beneficence, etc.: ambo nobis sint obnoxii, nostri devincti beneficio,; ; ; ; et saep.; cf.: suos praemiis, adversarios clementiae specie,: homines benevolentia et caritate,: virum sibi praestanti in eum liberalitate,: animos centurionum pignore, et saep.: aliquem omni cautione, foedere, exsecratione,: se cum aliquo affinitate,; cf. : ubi animus semel se cupiditate devinxit mala,; cf.: animum misericordia,: devinctus Domitiae nuptiis, : se vino,; cf.: animum ebrietate,: membra sopore,; cf. .—Hence, dē-vinctus, a, um, P. a., devoted, greatly attached to (very rare): quibus (studiis) uterque nostrum devinctus est,: studiis a pueritia dediti ac devincti,: uxori devinctus,: devinctior alicui,.

la:verb:devenio.gloss: to come down, descend; come from or to; arrive at (from somewhere), land at, reach
senses: to come down, descend; come from or to; arrive at (from somewhere), land at, reach
la:verb:devenio.html:
dē-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4,
v. n.; orig., to come from somewhere; hence, with predominant reference to the term. ad quem (cf. de, no. II. B.), to go to, arrive at, reach (class.).
Lit.: quomodo ad hunc devenerim In servitutem ab eo, etc.,; cf.: quam quisque in partem ab opere casu devenit,: ad alias aedes,: ad mare, id Poen. 3, 3, 14: ad legionem decimam,: in insidias,to fall,; cf.: in victoris manus,: in loca nobis adversa,: in eum locum,: in Scythiam,: domum alicujus,: quo, * et saep. —
Poet. with simple acc.: devenere locos ubi, etc.,; so, locos laetos,: speluncam eandem,; 166: silvas et amoena piorum,. Cf.: venio, pervenio, and 1. eo.—
Transf., in vulg. lang., like our to come, instead of to go to a place: deveniam ad lenonem domum egomet solus,: post ad furem ego devenio,; .—
Trop., to reach, arrive at, come to: tantum devenisse ad eum mali, *: ad juris studium,; cf. : devenit aut potius incidit in istum,; cf.: in medium rerum omnium certamen atque discrimen (coupled with incidere),: in alicujus tutelam,: in quos fines saeculorum,.

la:verb:devotus.gloss: vowed, promised, dedicated, having been vowed, devoted
senses: vowed, promised, dedicated, having been vowed, devoted

la:verb:devoto.html:
dē-vōto, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. intens. a. [id.].
To dedicate, devote (rare): et me dicabo atque animam devotabo hostibus, Att. ap. (but , read devota vita); and,
To bewitch, enchant: sortes,: devotatus defixusque, Ap. Herb. 7.—
To invoke with vows: numina, Ap. M. 9, p. 227, 4: asinos cum Iside, Minuc. Fel. Oct. 28, 5. —
To curse: se, Quaest. in Hept. 40.

la:verb:devolvo.gloss: to roll or tumble off or down
senses: to roll or tumble off or down
to roll, fall or tumble down, roll oneself down, fall headlong; sink down; devolve
la:verb:devolvo.html:
dē-volvo, volvi, vŏlūtum, 3,
v. a., to roll or tumble down (class.).
Lit.: saxa in musculum,, and 2; cf. saxa (amnis),: auratas trabes,: tonitrua, i. e. to imitate it (by rolling down balls behind the scenes), : clipeos e muris,: panem ex igne,: corpora in humum,: se toris, et saep.—Poet.: fusis mollia pensa,i. e. to spin off,.—
Pass. in mid. force, to roll itself down, to roll or tumble down, to fall headlong: monte praecipiti devolutus torrens,; cf. ; : jumenta cum oneribus devolvebantur,: ex praecipiti,.—
Trop.: aliquem vitā suā, to remove from,i. e. to deprive of,: per audaces nova dithyrambos Verba devolvit (the figure being taken from a river),.—
Mid., to sink down, fall into: ad spem inanem pacis devoluti, * : retro ad stirpem,: ad otium et inertiam, prooem. § 29: devolvuntur,hasten down,.

la:verb:devolo.html:
dē-vŏlo, āre,
v. n., to fly down or away (very rare).
Lit.
To fly down: devolant angues jubati deorsum in impluvium,: Iris per caelum,: sibi de caelo devolaturam in sinum victoriam,.—
To fly away: turdus devolet illuc, ubi, etc.,: phoenicem devolavisse in Aegyptum,.—
Transf., to hasten down, to fly or hasten away: de tribunali,: in terram,: praecipites in forum,; cf.: raptim ad puerum,: ab afflicta amicitia transfugere atque ad florentem aliam devolare, * ; cf. absol. .

la:verb:devoveo.gloss: to vow, offer; promise; devote, dedicate
senses: to vow, offer; promise; devote, dedicate
to bewitch, curse (by devoting to the infernal gods)
la:verb:devoveo.html:
dē-vŏvĕo, vōvi, vōtum, 2, v. a.
To vow, devote (usually to a deity).
Prop. (class.): Marti ea, quae bello ceperint,; so, Dianae pulcherrimum,: gnatam pro muta agna, et saep.; esp. freq.: se diis, or simply se,to devote one's self to death, to sacrifice one's self,; : se pro aere alieno, in jesting allusion to the death of the Decii,: se pro patria Quiritibusque Romanis,; ; ; : devota vita,; cf.: devotis corporibus in hostem ruentes,: ancipiti deum irae devotus,: hinc Remus auspicio se devovet, Enn. ap. : devota morti pectora,; cf. without morti: stabat devota juventus,: caput pro salute alicujus,, extr. 2 et saep.—
Transf., to devote, give up, attach (rarely): vobis animam hanc devovi,; cf.: suos annos soli tibi,; esp.: se, to give one's self up to, devote one's self to: se amicitiae alicujus,; cf.: se gloriae,: se regibus,.—
To promise solemnly, vow; with inf. or obj. clause (late Lat.): qui se devoverunt, nec manducare nec bibere,: totam vitam suam serviturum se esse devovit,; Gregor. M. Homil. 1, 19, 7.—
To mark out, destine, appoint: exspectatione omnium T. Annio devota et constituta ista hostia esse videtur,.—
Qs. to devote to the infernal gods, i. e. to curse, to execrate (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose—for syn. cf. detestor): aliquem,: natum suum (Theseus),: se ipse,: scelerata arma,: suas artes,: devota arbos,: devoti sanguinis aetas, et saep.; v. such a form of imprecation in .—
To bewitch by conjurations (poet.): aliquem carminibus, pollentibus herbis,: aliquem trajectis lanis,; cf.: devota veneno corpora,. —Hence, dēvōtus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to no. I. B.).
Devoted to any one, i. e. attached, faithful (post-Aug.): ni tibi deditus essem Devotusque cliens,; so with deditus,: devotissimus alicui,; cf. ; and: DEVOTISSIMVS NVMINI MAIESTATIQVE EIVS,; and so in comp., : animus alicui devotus, Tiber. ap. : equester ordo scenae harenaeque devotus,.—Poet.: devotae in externa proelia dextrae,ready for,.—Subst.: cum DC devotis, quos illi Soldurios appellant,with six hundred faithful followers,. —
In Christian authors, pious, devout: Roma Deo,: filia Christo,: jejunia,; so, obedient to authority, .—
Like deditus, given to, abandoned to a habit or thing (rare): vino,.—Adv.: dēvōtē, devotedly, faithfully: devote ac strenue, Cod. Th. 6, 24, 10.—Sup.: Deo devotissime serviamus,;

la:verb:devio.html:
dē-vĭo, āvi, 1,
v. n., to turn from the straight road, to go aside, to deviate (late Lat.; for de via declinare or devertere).
Prop., ; —
Trop., ; : a vero,.

la:verb:devito.html:
dē-vīto, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to avoid, go out of the way of, shun (rare but class.): illos fluctus,; cf.: procellam temporis,: malum,: letum,: dolorem,: exiguum censum turpemque repulsam,: suspicionem,: δυσφημίαν nominis, : stultitiam,.

la:verb:devoro.gloss: to swallow, gulp down, or devour; enjoy
senses: to swallow, gulp down, or devour; enjoy
to swallow down, repress, suppress, check, bear with patience
la:verb:devoro.html:
dē-vŏro, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to swallow, swallow down, gulp down, devour (class.; esp. freq. in transf. signif.—for syn. cf.: edo, comedo, vescor, pascor, mando).
Lit., of the physical act: id quod devoratur,: ovum gallinaceum integrum,: laseris paululum,

: salivam suam,; lapides,: succum,: fumum, et saep.—

Transf.
Of inanimate subjects, to swallow up, ingulf, absorb: devorer telluris hiatu,: terra devoravit montem,: vel me Charybdis devoret,: terras devorant aquae,: sol aquas devorans,: ne rotae devorarentur (viarum mollitudine),.—
To seize upon greedily or hastily, to swallow eagerly, to devour: meretricem ego item esse reor, mare ut est; quod des, devorat,: spe et opinione praedam,; cf.: spe devoratum lucrum,; and: regis hereditatem spe,: aliquid oculis,; cf.: spectat oculis devorantibus draucos,; cf. infra III. B.—
To swallow down, repress, suppress, check: verborum pars devorari solet, to be swallowed, i. e. only half pronounced, ; so, verba, Sen. de Ira, 3, 14 fin.; cf. lacrimas,i. e. to repress,; : gemitus,—
Of property, to consume, to waste, = exhaurire: omnem pecuniam publicam,; ; .—And with a pers. object: Si. Jamne illum comesurus es? Ba. Dum recens est, Dum datur, dum calet, devorari decet, ; ; cf.: ut hominem devorari, cujus patrimonium consumitur, .—
Trop., to consume, destroy: devorent vos arma vestra,; cf.: aquilarum pinnae reliquarum alitum pinnas devorant,: vox devoratur,i. e. is swallowed up, lost,: devoravi nomen imprudens, swallowed, i. e. I have lost, utterly forgotten, : devorato pudore, Ap. M. 9, p. 225.—
Trop.
To swallow any thing unpleasant, i. e to bear patiently, to endure: hominum ineptias ac stultitias,; so, molestiam paucorum dierum,: taedium illud,: bilem et dolorem, Tert. Res. carn. 54.—
To accept eagerly, enjoy: quid tibi faciam qui illos libros devorasti,: os impiorum devorat iniquitatem,: auscultate et mea dicta devorate,; cf.: orationem dulcem (aures),: verbum ipsum (voluptatis),.—
ejus oratio, nimia religione attenuata, a multitudine et a foro devorabatur, qs. swallowed but not digested (i. e. heard without being understood), .

la:adv:devote.html:
dēvōtē,
adv., devotedly, faithfully, v. devoveo, P. a. fin.

la:verb:devinco.gloss: to defeat decisively, subdue, conquer, triumph
senses: to defeat decisively, subdue, conquer, triumph
la:verb:devinco.html:
dē-vinco, vīci, victum, 3,
v. a., to conquer completely, overcome, subdue.
Prop. (class.; for syn. cf.: vinco, supero, fundo, fugo, profligo, subigo, subicio, domo): Galliam Germaniamque,; ; : devincere et capere Capuam,: Poenos classe,; cf.: Crotoniatas maximo proelio,: Sabaeae reges,: serpentem,: flumina, et saep.—With ut and subj.: Catonis sententia devicit, ut in decreto perstaretur,.— Poet.: devicta bella,victoriously concluded,.—
Trop.: hominum consilia,: bonum publicum privatā gratiā devictum,sacrificed to,.

la:verb:devello.html:
dē-vello, velli, vulsum, (
perf. devolsit, ), 3, v. a., to pluck down, to pull or tear off (very rare; not in Cic. and Caes.): pennas, Plaut, Poen. 4, 2, 50; cf.: plumam anseribus,: plantas de matrum radice,: effigies (sc. in Tiberim; cf. , and ), . In an obscene sense: concubinas (i. e. depilare),.

la:verb:deverro.html:
dē-verro (dīv-), ĕre,
v. a., to sweep away, sweep out (very rare): devorare omnia ac deverrere, Lucil. ap. ; Varr. ap. ; .

ejus oratio, nimia religione attenuata, a multitudine et a foro devorabatur, qs. swallowed but not digested (i. e. heard without being understood), .

senses: to carry away (by river or sea)
la:verb:deveho.html:
dē-vĕho, xi, ctum, 3,
v. a., to carry down, to carry, convey, take away.
Prop. (class.; most freq. in the histt.): has (carinas) carris junctis devehit noctu milia passuum a castris XXII.,: legionem equis,: maximos commeatus (Tiberis), : id simulacrum Syracusis,: devecta cremato Sarmenta, * et saep.—Designating the term. ad quem: aliquem in Anactorium,: quod (frumentum) eo tolerandae hiemis causa devexerat,; cf. : tritici decies centum milia ad mare,: frumentum in Graeciam,: saucios in oppidum, et saep.—
Pass. in middle sense, to go away, to go down, descend: Veliam devectus Brutum vidi, *: Tiberi devectus,; cf. Rheno,: Arare flumine,: Misenum usque devectus, et saep.—
Trop.: nunc ad tua devehar astra,

senses: A place for travellers to put up; an inn, lodging.
la:noun:deverticulum.html:
dēvertĭcŭlum (many MSS. and some edd. dīvert-, old form dēvort-), i, n.
deverto
.
A by-road, by-path, side-way.
Prop.: quae deverticula flexionesque quaesivisti?; ; ; ; ; : fluminis,a branch,; .—
Trop., a deviation, digression: legentibus velut deverticula amoena quaerere,; cf. ; : aquarum calidarum, i. e. a mode of cure (deviating from the simple one) by the use of warm water, : significationis,derivation,in lemm.: a deverticulo repetatur fabula,from the digression,: per varia sectarum deverticula,byways of doctrine,.—
A place for travellers to put up; an inn, a lodging.
Prop.: cum gladii abditi ex omnibus locis deverticuli protraherentur,; also, a resort for low characters: lupanaria et deverticula,.—
Trop., a refuge, retreat, lurking-place, ; ; ; ; .

la:noun:devotio.gloss: The act of devoting or consecrating.
senses: The act of devoting or consecrating.
The act of cursing; curse, imprecation, execration.
Sorcery, enchantment; magical formula, incantation, spell.
la:noun:devotio.html:
dēvōtĭo, ōnis, f.
devoveo
.
A devoting, consecrating.
Prop.: Deciorum devotiones,the devoting of themselves,; cf. vitae,; capitis,; a vow, . —
Transf., fealty, allegiance, devotedness (late Lat.): alicujus erga rempublicam, Treb. Poll. Gall. 14: Aquileiensium pro Romanis, et Balb. 11: quis fortes animat devotio mentes,—Hence,
(Cf. devotus, P. a. no. B.) In Christian authors, piety, devotion, zeal, : inutilis est Deo qui devotione caret,; cf. coupled with religio,.—
A cursing, curse, imprecation, execration, : pilae in quibus devotio fuerit scripta,: dissimulata nauseantis devotione,; v. also .—
Sorcery, enchantment; and concr., a magical formula, incantation, spell, : carmina et devotiones,; : devotionibus et veneno peremisse,; 4, 52: conjugium (i. e. conjugem) principis devotionibus petere, al.—
Transf., any form of prayer: devotiones faustae, Ap. M. 11, p. 265, 5.

la:verb:devoco.html:
dē-vŏco, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to call off, call away; also to call down.—With abl. of the place whence after de, ab, ex, rarely without a prep.; and with reference to the term. ad quem (cf. de, no. II. B.), to call, to fetch by calling to any place, with ad or in (rare but class.).
Lit.: aliquem de provincia ... ad gloriam, ad triumphum, etc.,: suos ab tumulo,; cf.: ex praesidiis,: refixa sidera caelo,; cf.: Jovem caelo sacrificio,; and: Jovem deosque alios ad auxilium,: aliquem in judicium,; cf.: aliquem in certamen,: aliquem (ad cenam),to invite,. —
Trop., to call off, allure, call down, etc.: non (illum) avaritia ab instituto cursu ad praedam aliquam devocavit, non libido ad voluptatem, etc.,; cf.: huc a simulacris deorum hominumque humanissimam artem, Sill.: philosophiam e caelo,: suas fortunas in dubium, to endanger, * ; cf.: aliquem in id, ut, etc., to prevail on one to, etc., : mortales ad perniciem,to bring,: rem ad populum,.
